messages:
elaine: FYI I saw a sharp rise in router queue_depth during a multi-flag apply from the console this morning. some pools momentarily hit 95% worker utilization. attaching minimal logs.

elaine: ```
[2026-03-23T09:03:11Z] apply-run: id=INF-8551 user=nina scope=tenant:42 flags=73
[2026-03-23T09:03:12Z] apply-orch: enqueued shards=12 total_tasks=614
[2026-03-23T09:03:13Z] router-us-west-2: queue_depth=580 capacity=600 workers_active=48
[2026-03-23T09:03:14Z] quota-svc: throttle=true backoff=exponential
[2026-03-23T09:03:15Z] apply-run: paused auto_pause=true reason=high_pool_load
```

chris: ouch. did the preview estimator flag this?

nina: we used the preview but the cohort sampling missed this tenant. also the console default parallelism was bumped to 32 in that org-level template last month.

ops-bot: incident: router-pool us-west-2 spike — incident-2026-03-23-002 created.

sam: Proposal: add an "apply preflight estimator" endpoint and two small schema fields under apply_controls: max_parallelism (int), shard_window_ms (int). console should call estimator before sending the real apply.

chris: agree. estimator should take scope (tenant ids / flags) and a desired parallelism and return an estimated peak_concurrency and risk_score. risk_score = peak_concurrency / pool_capacity. if > 0.8 mark high.

elaine: technically we can compute peak_concurrency from route_count * cohort_factor / parallelism, but need to account for hot shards — use router telemetry (worker_capacity_by_shard) to make it conservative.

nina: UX: console shows estimate inline with an option "auto-adjust to safe defaults" which would lower parallelism to something safe per-pool. also surface a suggestion: "split apply into N batches".

chris: API sketch: POST /v1/apply/estimate body {"scope":"tenant:42","parallelism":16} -> {"estimated_peak":420,"pool_capacity":600,"risk":"medium","suggested_parallelism":8}. Make estimator idempotent and cheap (use cached shard metrics).

sam: runtime: apply orchestrator will accept apply_controls.* fields and implement token-bucket gating per router-pool. it should also emit telemetry: apply.estimate.risk, apply.fanout.batch_size, apply.fanout.inflight_per_pool.

elaine: operations note: auto-pause behavior should create a paused state with explicit recovery steps (reduce parallelism / resume). by default auto-pause=true for non-admins. enterprise tenants can opt into stricter controls via policy.

nina: can we include the estimator call in the dry-run path so owners see risk during preview?

chris: yes. dry-run should surface estimator output and a small red/yellow/green risk pill. add preview flag estimate=true to existing endpoint.

sam: timeline: I'll prototype token-bucket gating and telemetry in 4 days. chris will add API schema changes and estimator endpoint in 5 days. nina will update console UX once API is stable (7 days).

elaine: action items:
- sam: implement gating + telemetry (due 2026-03-27)
- chris: estimator endpoint + schema + tests (due 2026-03-28)
- nina: console risk UI + auto-adjust flow (due 2026-03-30)
- elaine: ops runbook update + incident postmortem note (due 2026-03-29)

sam: question  should we add a backoff_strategy enum (linear/exponential) to apply_controls? useful for retry behavior on auto-pause.

chris: yes include backoff_strategy with default=linear. implement as metadata only initially.

nina: okay tagging INF-8551 in the project board and will link to the incident.

elaine: thanks all, will watch for the prototype. leaving thread open for updates. :eyes:
